searchText: > update gas_premium such that it is a function of block size or uncle rate instead of a flat value. How do users express their urgency preference in this case ? The same way as they do now, or through something like escalating fee or whatever. Ideally, something like a uniform price auction would be nice but the specifics I don't think are relevant to the general concept. who's doing the "update" in the quoted sentence above? At the moment, I believe most (all?) Ethereum mining clients just hard-code the miner fee. The idea would be to update the clients so they utilize a smarter algorithm. At the moment, blocks are full with transactions at 40 nanoeth gas price sitting in the pending queue. Miners should be willing to risk bigger blocks (which means more uncles) in exchange for 40 nanoeth per gas, but their mining software is dumb and is throwing away free money because they just have a hard-coded gas price and block size. Also, individual miners cannot choose different block sizes, it is just a majority "vote" for block size, which is just humans weighted by hashpower making arbitrary decisions. gas_premium is a user thing, the "tip" in 1559, or are you referring to something else ? Sorry, I meant "gas destined for miners", I was using `gas_premium` from 1559 as a shorthand for that. Different from "gas that is burned".
